The project forms part of the municipality’s strategic spatial planning initiatives aimed at facilitating structured urban growth, improving land development opportunities, and promoting integrated settlement development within the Bizana urban area. The proposed development area is located on portions of the Remainder of Erf 110, Bizana Municipal Commonage, and has been identified by the municipality as a suitable area for future urban expansion and mixed -use development. The proposed township establishment is envisaged to accommodate a combination of residential, commercial, institutional, and supporting land uses in line with the spatial restructuring objectives of the municipality. Property Description The proposed development site is situated within the southeastern extent of Bizana, headed to Umhlanga Location and forms part of municipal commonage land under the ownership and administration of the Winnie Madikizela -Mandela Local Municipality. The area is strategically located within proximity to existing urban development and key movement routes, making it suitable for future township establishment and urban expansion. The baseline study is intended to establish a clear understanding of the existing spatial, environmental, cadastral, infrastructural, and land use conditions affecting the site and to determine the suitability of the land for future township establishment. Currently, the municipality does not have sufficient baseline information and technical assessments to guide informed decision-making regarding the development potential, spatial structuring, and implementation requirements of the proposed mixed -use township. The absence of this information limits the municipality’s ability to effectively plan for future urban expansion, infrastructure investment, and coordinated land development within the southeastern portion of Bizana. Currently, the municipality does not have sufficient baseline information and technical assessments to guide informed decision-making regarding the development potential, spatial structuring, and implementation requirements of the proposed mixed -use township. The absence of this information limits the municipality’s ability to effectively plan for future urban expansion, infrastructure investment, and coordinated land development within the southeastern portion of Bizana. Furthermore, the area may be affected by various development constraints, including, environmental considerations, servicing limitations, and legislative compliance 8 requirements, all of which require detailed investigation prior to the commencement of township planning processes. The undertaking of a baseline study will therefore enable the municipality to: * Assess the suitability and feasibility of the site for mixed-use township establishment, * Identify development opportunities and constraints, * Inform future township layout planning and infrastructure requirements, * Ensure alignment with the WMMLM SDF (2025), SPLUMA, and other applicable planning legislation, and * Prepare the municipality for subsequent phases of planning, including township establishment

The undertaking of a baseline study will therefore enable the municipality to: * Assess the suitability and feasibility of the site for mixed-use township establishment, * Identify development opportunities and constraints, * Inform future township layout planning and infrastructure requirements, * Ensure alignment with the WMMLM SDF (2025), SPLUMA, and other applicable planning legislation, and * Prepare the municipality for subsequent phases of planning, including township establishment processes, engineering assessments, and land development implementation. This project therefore seeks to undertake comprehensive baseline investigations and planning assessments for the proposed mixed-use township establishment within the southeastern portion of Bizana in order to support future development planning and implementation readiness. 3. The scope of work entails undertaking baseline studies and preliminary planning assessments for the proposed mixed -use township establishment within the southeastern portion of Bizana, and the surveying, zoning and registration of municipal sites/properties and will also be subject to the need and desirability to conduct surveying project The scope shall include, but not be limited to, the following: * Collection and review of existing spatial, cadastral, and land use information; * Assessment of applicable planning policies and legislative frameworks, including alignment with the WMMLM SDF (2025); * Site analysis and identification of development opportunities and constraints; * High -level assessment of environmental, topographical, and land suitability considerations; * Investigation of existing land tenure and cadastral information; 9 * Assessment of surrounding land uses and urban integration opportunities; * Preliminary identification of infrastructure and service-related considerations; * Preparation of a baseline analysis report and development informants plan; * Recommendations to guide future township establishment and layout planning processes.

The proposed township establishment is envisaged to accommodate a combination of residential, commercial, institutional, and supporting land uses in line with the spatial restructuring objectives of the municipality. Property Description The proposed development site is situated within the southeastern extent of Bizana, headed to Umhlanga Location and forms part of municipal commonage land under the ownership and administration of the Winnie Madikizela -Mandela Local Municipality. The area is strategically located within proximity to existing urban development and key movement routes, making it suitable for future township establishment and urban expansion. xtent of Bizana, headed to Umhlanga Location and forms part of municipal commonage land under the ownership and administration of the Winnie Madikizela -Mandela Local Municipality. The area is strategically located within proximity to existing urban development and key movement routes, making it suitable for future township establishment and urban expansion. Apart from limited pockets of privately -owned land within the Bizana urban area, a significant portion of land within the Winnie Madikizela -Mandela Local Municipality remains state-owned or held in trust by the Minister responsible for Rural Development and Land Reform. Land ownership and tenure arrangements within the municipal area are often characterised by complex land administration systems and overlapping land rights. Furthermore, various portions of land within the Bizana urban area remain affected by land claim processes lodged in terms of the Restitution of Land Rights Act, 22 of 1994.
